title: The inference domain answers who asks for its calls
intention: Any device can ask the inference domain over the bus for its stored calls, most recent first, bounded by a limit and a since-time, without importing the domain; the domain stays ignorant of what the asker does with them.
why: Measured 2026-10-13 by the builder while building 95f8c561e742 (the librarian deposits resolved inference calls as nodes): the reader face domain.read_ticket (cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py:721) is not in the device's declared interface (public_interface is only cairn.devices.inference_domain.host) and no bus verb or view reaches it (verbs resolve/embed/infer, views yield/models; device.py:38-53). So a consumer that honours RULE 1 has nothing to call. A view takes no arguments (_yield_view(self)), so the ask is a verb.
traces_to: RULE 1 (a consumer reaches a device only through its declared interface; this widens the interface instead of letting the librarian reach in) and Law 1 (the stored calls are already answered questions; a reader face lets them become structure instead of being re-asked).
how: cairn/devices/inference_domain only. (a) domain.read_ticket gains a keyword since: str | None = None (ISO timestamp); rows with created <= since are dropped before the limit is applied. (b) InferenceDomainDevice.declared_verbs adds 'calls': self._handle_calls, which reads body.get('limit') (default 100, capped at 1000) and body.get('since') and returns {'calls': [...]} from read_ticket, each row made JSON-safe (datetimes to isoformat) so it crosses the bus. (c) the charter's public_interface names the 'calls' verb beside host.
falsifier: cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_the_domain_answers_for_its_calls.py under PROVES {'b905340f8162': {'1','2','3','4'}} over a scratch inference_calls table seeded with three rows at known created times: (1) 'calls' is in InferenceDomainDevice().declared_verbs(); (2) the handler with body {'limit': 2} returns the two newest rows, newest first; (3) with body {'since': <the oldest row's created>} it returns only the two later rows; (4) json.dumps of the reply succeeds. Hollow: today's device.py and domain.py red 1-4.

intent_berth: none, because this is a bug entering as a ticket (skills/intent/SKILL.md, the TICKET entry point), born from the measured fault at /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/cairn/devices/inference_domain/device.py

decisions.text: A verb, not a view: a view takes no arguments and the ask needs limit and since. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
No NOTIFY is added here: the librarian exposes ingest as its own verb (95f8c561e742), so nothing polls and no event is invented before it has a receiver. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
95f8c561e742 builds only the librarian side and depends on this ticket; its build waits for this one at PROVED. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

Write cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_the_domain_answers_for_its_calls.py FIRST (red first) with PROVES = {'b905340f8162': {'1','2','3','4'}} mapped to four teeth over a scratch table from domain.scratch_cache('calls_verb') seeded with three rows at known created times via store.write(table, domain.CACHE_OWNER, row): (1) 'calls' is in InferenceDomainDevice().declared_verbs() and some entry of the charter's public_interface contains 'calls'; (2) body {limit: 2} returns the two newest rows, newest first; (3) since = the oldest row's created returns the two later rows, since = the newest returns []; (4) json.dumps of the reply succeeds. The teeth call InferenceDomainDevice()._handle_calls({'body': body}, table=<scratch>). Measured 2026-10-13: all four red on today's code. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09; approved thru PROVED (Akien 2026-10-12)

In cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py, read_ticket gains the keyword 'since: str | None = None' (placed before table). After the existing sort (most recent first) and BEFORE the limit, when since is given, keep only rows whose created is strictly later than since. Both sides are compared as aware UTC datetimes: a small helper _as_utc(when) parses an ISO string with datetime.fromisoformat and takes a naive value as UTC. Canonical, table and conn behave as today. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09; approved thru PROVED (Akien 2026-10-12)

In cairn/devices/inference_domain/device.py, declared_verbs adds 'calls': self._handle_calls. _handle_calls(self, envelope, *, table=None) reads body = envelope['body'] (or {}), limit = clamp(int(body.get('limit') or 100), 1, 1000), since = body.get('since'), calls domain.read_ticket(limit=limit, since=since, table=table when given), and returns {'calls': [_json_safe(row) for row in rows]}. It needs no connection of its own: read_ticket opens and closes one when conn is None, and the table defaults to domain.CACHE (inference_calls). The table kwarg is a proof seam only; the bus never passes it. A module-level _json_safe(value) walks dicts and lists, turning datetime/date into isoformat() and Decimal (cost) into float. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09; approved thru PROVED (Akien 2026-10-12)

Append ONE prose entry to public_interface in cairn/devices/inference_domain/intention+why.json (the existing 'cairn.devices.inference_domain.host' stays): "bus verb 'calls' (ticket b905340f8162): body {limit (default 100, cap 1000), since (ISO)} -> {'calls': [inference_calls rows, most recent first, JSON-safe]}; the domain does not know who asks". Written through bin/cairn artifact write --verb charter, then cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh in the same act. Prose entries are allowed in public_interface. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09; approved thru PROVED (Akien 2026-10-12)
decisions.step: Step 4: the charter names the verb

decisions.text: The verb takes no connection or table from the caller: read_ticket opens its own connection when conn is None and reads domain.CACHE (inference_calls) by default; canonical is not used by this verb (recency order, bounded by limit and since). See Step 3. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09; approved thru PROVED (Akien 2026-10-12)
